notes: the second motor through the same estimators as mg90-b's file, every input re-derived from mg90-c's own captures in this notebook, since no mg90-c bemf-coast result existed when it ran: the per-spin list (spin speed in the current's ripple over the spin's last 200 ms, i_spin_a through current-scale's in-drive offset, i_spin_open_zero_a through the coast's tail, v_on_v, the dropouts) as bemf-coast reads it; ke_v_s_per_rad is bemf-coast's coast route, the EMF over the whole ripple cycles closest to 10 ms from 1 ms past the cut over the speed counted in the same rows, open rows bridged, the mean over the spins with a counted window under the rest zero, its bounds the same mean under no zero and under the coast's tail only (bemf-coast's rail split and estimator share are not read here); reading_term_a_per_v is this motor's meter-1, the crest sample over the DMM in series per volt of the terminal difference, the mean at 20 to 40 % with the three points as the bounds, and the _meter keys take the term by duty through meter-1's 20, 30 and 40 % points and high-1's 60, 80 and 100 % points on 5.0 V, held below 20 %, the same per volt on every rail; the meter runs were captured after the motor's brushes changed at 7.4 V and capture-1 before, and the term is carried across that on the assumption that it is a property of the drive and the leads. The ladder has three rails, 3.7, 5.0 and 7.4 V, so the per-level keys carry three levels; level_gap keys stay 7.4 V over the 5.0 V curve as in mg90-b's file; the one-J lines and the bracket take the 3.7 V rungs in. j_kg_m2's bounds run from the lowest to the highest of the term-out routes through the coast, the spin-up's line with the term out and the spin-up's ratio both ways, without the meter loop's R-L bias, which needs this motor's rest-resistance and inductance results. Everything else as in mg90-b's notes

3.7 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s, the board's crest reading with the reading term in, not the drag; the drag is drive_drag_by_level_meter

5 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s, the board's crest reading with the reading term in, not the drag; the drag is drive_drag_by_level_meter

7.4 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s, the board's crest reading with the reading term in, not the drag; the drag is drive_drag_by_level_meter

level_gap_a.unit: A, 7.4 V over the 5.0 V curve at the same speed

coast_decel_late_rad_s2.form: alpha = a + b sqrt(w), w in rad/s

coast_relax_early_pct.unit: % over the late curve in the first 8 ms, 5 ms windows; the bounds span the 5 and 10 ms windows

reading_term_a_per_v.unit: A per V of the terminal difference at the crest sample

3.7 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s; drag torque = Kt x I0; the reading term taken out, the drag under drive

5 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s; drag torque = Kt x I0; the reading term taken out, the drag under drive

7.4 V.form: I0 = a + b ln(w / w_ref), w in rad/s, w_ref = 2 pi x 100 rad/s; drag torque = Kt x I0; the reading term taken out, the drag under drive

level_gap_meter_a.unit: A, 7.4 V over the 5.0 V curve at the same speed, the reading term taken out
